doc.title: Derek Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995

title: Joe Williams's singing
summary: Smith describes Joe Williams's tenor-like timbre and melodic phrasing.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: Have you had occasion to perform with Joe Williams?

Well, on the same stage. I haven’t—because he’s usually had Norman Simmons playing for him, even if I’m the studio pianist in the orchestra, you know, he’s got his own piano player. But I’ve known Joe all these years, and always been a fan of his.
How do you feel his voice is, typifies jazz vocals?

Well, he sounds to me like a good tenor player playing. It’s something in the timbre of his voice. It’s, I don’t know how to describe that either, but it’s something in the timbre. You know there’s an art to singing or playing a melody. It sort of becomes, not just acceptable but brilliant. And Joe’s got that, effortlessly. And really he’s not playing hot
like Frank Wess is playing hot, but you know if you hear Frank playing the melody, and it’s beautiful. And Joe is playing around the melody.
Yeah, we heard that last night, actually, one of his ballads.
